    Biography
    I'm a conservation technologist and ecologist. My work asks how technology can improve how we monitor wildlife and habitats, and how best to integrate remote sensing and conservation technology workflows into conservation planning decisions.
    I lecture in Ecology at the University of South Wales. I am Course Leader for the new MSc Conservation Technology and Ecological Data Science, launching in 2028, and Associate Editor for Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation and Methods in Ecology and Evolution.

  ResearchAll research →










Acoustics


Passive acoustic monitoring of wildlife, from horseshoe bats to large carnivores, and low-cost networked sensors that bring sound data in from the field.












Earth observation


Satellite, drone and laser-scanning data for mapping habitats and land-use change, and understanding how error in these maps affects conservation decisions.












Microclimate ecology


How vegetation structure shapes the fine-scale climates animals actually live in, measured with sensor networks and 3D forest scans.












Thermal biology


Operative temperature, thermal preference and thermal habitat for tropical reptiles, and how warming changes the habitat available to them.












Movement ecology


GPS tracking and step-selection models to understand how large mammals such as elephants and carnivores use space.












Machine learning in conservation


Machine learning that links remote sensing and sensor data to field measurements, to predict species, habitats and conditions across whole landscapes.












Computer vision


Automated detection, species classification and individual identification from camera-trap images.












Ethics of conservation technology


How conservation data and technology can be misused, and how protected areas can reduce those risks.

title: Teaching
text: I teach ecology, conservation biology, statistics, remote sensing and conservation technology at undergraduate and postgraduate level at the University of South Wales, with a strong emphasis on fieldwork and hands-on data collection.

Collaborators
I’m always keen to hear from researchers, conservation organisations, protected area managers and technology developers who are interested in working together. title: Code
text:
Open workflows for ecological remote sensing, movement and sensor data.
